result.title: How We’ll Actually Ditch Fossil Fuels — by the Numbers | Michael Liebreich | TED
result.description:
Have you heard the clean energy transition is failing? Energy analyst Michael Liebreich says to look again. Using a four-line spreadsheet model of the global energy system, he shows why fossil fuels will inevitably get squeezed out over time — with no bans required. The shift is well underway, he explains: it just looks different than many of us expected. (Recorded at TED Countdown: The Next Ten on October 15, 2026)

result.title: "Deep listening” can help you form relationships across generations, cultures and divides #TEDTalks
result.description: Do you avoid talking to people you disagree with? Author and mediator Emily Kasriel thinks you should try it out. She explains why engaging with ideas that bother you is one of the most powerful things you can do — and presents her framework for “deep listening” that can help you form relationships across generations, cultures and political divides.

result.title: The harder you try to control everything, the more likely you are to get in your own way #TEDTalks
result.description: When life gets uncertain, do you grip a little tighter? Neuroscientist Heather Berlin explores a surprising paradox: the harder you try to control everything, the more likely you are to get in your own way. Drawing on brain research and her own struggles with uncertainty, she shares practical ways to let go and make room for creativity, calm and flow.

result.title: How to Teach a Robot to Dance | David Dobáš | TED
result.description:
Teaching a robot to dance, move or even stand up used to take countless hours of training. Now, by simply recording a video, you can teach a robot a new skill in a fraction of the time, says roboticist David Dobáš. In a live demo with TED guest curator Bilawal Sidhu, Dobáš shows how advances in AI are transforming the way these humanoid machines learn — and proves it with a robot dance performance at the end.(Recorded at David Dobáš on April 17, 2026)
